common_spatial_measures_q25.scope: Common tangent tensors embedded with zero normal stress and zero transverse shear define both peak invariants. This is distinct from each method's raw full3D peak. Identical angular rays sample every unioned tetrahedron boundary on both sides, outer/inner boundaries and depth Gauss nodes; surface/depth sampling convergence remains required. Positions are on the common reference rest columns. Normal and transverse shear components are integrated separately with the field metric weights; Shell lacks these independent 3D components and receives no transverse error rank.

scope: Nine normal-pad comparisons. RMS uses the Frobenius tensor norm, full physical volume for tangent stress, and full mid-surface area for membrane, bending and boundary fibers. Membrane and bending use the original declared 500um material thickness. All retained columns are included without trimming. Reference surface RMS is derived from the already integrated absolute/relative pair, not independently reintegrated. Fields use q9/depth2 and common peaks use q25; raw peaks keep their original distinct samplings. Full3D-only components and peak locations remain in details; the saved raw position is the raw Mises location, not a tensile location. No near-zero floor is used: every reference normalization is positive. Existing conditional uncertainty/ranks remain unchanged; this is no new continuum qualification.
